```{r}
#| label: load-data

# Small tidy files produced by R/02_clean_data.R live in data/
# example <- read_csv(here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "example.csv"))

# Crime Severity Index and violent CSI, 1998 on, for Canada, Ontario and
# Waterloo Region (labelled "Region", cwr_region). One row per place per year.
csi_comparison <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "csi_comparison.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Rates per 100,000 people of nine assault and sexual offences for Canada,
# Ontario and the Region, each also indexed to its base year (100 = the
# base-year rate). One row per offence per place per year. UCR codes are read
# as text: they are labels, and "130" and "1310" are different offences.
crime_rates <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "crime_rates.csv"),
  col_types = cols(ucr_code = col_character())
)

# Share of Kitchener residents who said each type of crime had increased over
# the past year, with the survey's 95% margin of error as lower and upper
# bounds (Liaison Strategies, October 2025). One row per type of crime.
crime_perception <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "crime_perception.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  clean_names()
```

<!-- Opening paragraph: the question this post asks and the one-line answer. -->

## First finding as a plain-language heading

<!-- One or two paragraphs, then one chart. -->

```{r}
#| label: crime-perception
#| output: asis

# Share of Kitchener residents who say each type of crime has increased over
# the past year, from Liaison Strategies' survey of 800 residents. Built from
# the ggdoterror template: each share is a dot, and the survey's 95% margin
# of error (plus or minus 3.46 points) is the fading bar behind it. The
# survey publishes one margin for the whole sample, not one per answer, so
# every bar is the same width (see R/02_clean_data.R).

# The seven Kitchener questions are sorted by share. "Crime in Canada" asked
# about the whole country, a different question, so it sits apart at the
# top and is drawn in red, the house colour for the Canada comparison.
perception_plot_data <- crime_perception |>
  mutate(
    sort_key = if_else(asked_about == "Canada", Inf, increased),
    crime = fct_reorder(crime, sort_key),
    colour = if_else(asked_about == "Canada", habsred, dodgerblue)
  )

p <- perception_plot_data |>
  ggplot(aes(y = crime)) +

  # The margin of error: a flat-ended bar from lower to upper bound, strongest
  # in the middle and fading to both ends. A tile is centred on x and as wide
  # as the interval; height is a share of the row. The gradient is a grid
  # pattern: group = FALSE runs it across each bar on its own, not across the
  # whole panel. Translucent, so gridlines show through. A pattern fill cannot
  # be mapped to a column, so the red Canada bar is its own layer.
  geom_tile(
    data = \(d) filter(d, asked_about == "Kitchener"),
    aes(x = (lower + upper) / 2, width = upper - lower),
    height = 0.24,
    fill = grid::linearGradient(
      colours = c(alpha(dodgerblue, 0.08), alpha(dodgerblue, 0.5), alpha(dodgerblue, 0.08)),
      group = FALSE
    )
  ) +
  geom_tile(
    data = \(d) filter(d, asked_about == "Canada"),
    aes(x = (lower + upper) / 2, width = upper - lower),
    height = 0.24,
    fill = grid::linearGradient(
      colours = c(alpha(habsred, 0.08), alpha(habsred, 0.5), alpha(habsred, 0.08)),
      group = FALSE
    )
  ) +

  # The share: a dot with a white rim so it stands off the bar
  geom_point(
    aes(x = increased, fill = colour),
    shape = 21, size = 4.5, stroke = 1,
    colour = "white"
  ) +

  scale_fill_identity() +

  # Percent of residents; the unit belongs in the subtitle (style rule 1c)
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(55, 75),   # the highest bound, robbery's, is 74.46
    breaks = seq(55, 75, 5),
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    position = "top"
  ) +

  # The row order is set here, not left to the layers: each tile layer sees
  # only some rows, and ggplot2 would otherwise order the rows in the order
  # the layers first meet them, which puts the rows out of order
  scale_y_discrete(
    position = "left",
    limits = levels(pull(perception_plot_data, crime))
  ) +

  # Horizontal chart: vertical gridlines only, no x ticks or axis line
  theme(
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Share of Kitchener residents who say crime has increased, by type of crime",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when",
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Liaison Strategies, Crime Perception in Ontario Cities",
      notes = "Bars show the survey's 95% margin of error, ±3.46 points",
      sample = "liaison_2025"
    )
  )

# Alt text built from the data, highest share first, so it cannot disagree
# with the dots
perception_alt <- perception_plot_data |>
  arrange(desc(sort_key)) |>
  mutate(entry = str_glue("{crime} {increased}%")) |>
  pull(entry) |>
  str_flatten_comma()

# On a phone, cwr_figure() wraps the names longer than "Crime in Canada" and
# deepens the rows to fit them (cwr_wrap_phone_labels() in theme_cwr.R)
cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-crime-perception",
  alt = str_glue(
    "Dot chart of the share of 800 Kitchener residents surveyed in October 2025 ",
    "who said each type of crime had increased over the past year, each with a ",
    "margin of error of plus or minus 3.46 points: {perception_alt}. ",
    "The first row asked about crime in Canada as a whole."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: csi

# Replicates the Globe and Mail's first chart (the Crime Severity Index for
# Canada) and adds Ontario and Waterloo Region. Built from the ggline template.
# Interactive: hovering near a line shows the place, year and index value.

# Colours carry the house meanings: Waterloo Region is the focus (blue), Canada
# the main comparison (red), Ontario context (grey). The Region is labelled
# with the house stock label, cwr_region ("Region").
csi_groups <- c("Canada", "Ontario", cwr_region)
csi_colours <- set_names(c(habsred, cowboysilver, dodgerblue), csi_groups)

# The tooltip text is built once per row, here, rather than in the ggplot call.
# ggiraph shows it as HTML, so <b> and <br> work. hover_id ties the two
# invisible point layers below together (see cwr_interactive() in theme_cwr.R).
csi_plot_data <- csi_comparison |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = csi_groups),
    hover_id = str_glue("{region}-{year}"),
    csi_tooltip = str_glue("<b>{region}</b><br>{year}<br>CSI: {label_number(accuracy = 0.1)(csi)}"),
    csi_violent_tooltip = str_glue("<b>{region}</b><br>{year}<br>Violent CSI: {label_number(accuracy = 0.1)(csi_violent)}")
  )

# Set x min and max
x_min <- csi_plot_data |> pull(year) |> min()
x_max <- csi_plot_data |> pull(year) |> max()

# Line-name labels. cwr_line_labels() sets each one's height from its own
# line: `at` is the year it is centred on, where that line has clear space,
# and `side` is the preferred side of the line. The helper switches sides if
# the preferred one would cover a gridline and the other is clear.
label_data <- cwr_line_labels(
  csi_plot_data, x = year, y = csi, group = region,
  at = set_names(c(2004, 2014, 2002), csi_groups),
  side = set_names(c("above", "below", "below"), csi_groups),
  limits = c(45, NA),   # the y scale's limits, so gridlines can be avoided
  bold = cwr_region
)

p <- ggplot(csi_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = csi, colour = region)) +

  geom_label(
    data = label_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fontface = fontface, vjust = vjust),
    colour = "grey30",
    fill = "white",
    linewidth = 0,
    size = 3.2,
    hjust = 0.5,     # centred on the year given in `at`
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Small invisible dots that appear on hover to mark the year...
  geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id = hover_id), size = 2.5, alpha = 0) +
  # ...under large invisible squares that catch the mouse anywhere near a line
  # and carry the tooltip. The squares go on top: a dot drawn over them would
  # take the mouse at the very point a reader aims for, and it has no tooltip.
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = csi_tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
    shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 5),
    labels = label_number(big.mark = "", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05)),
    position = "bottom"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(45, NA),   # room under the lowest line for a label
    position = "right",
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = csi_colours,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +

  # Right-axis label positioning: sit labels above gridlines
  theme(
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      size = rel(1),
      hjust = 1.0,
      vjust = -0.5,
      margin = margin(r = 12, l = -20)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when<br>",
    caption = cwr_caption(c("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0026-01", "Table 35-10-0188-01"))
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-csi",
  alt = paste(
    "Line chart of the Crime Severity Index from", x_min, "to", x_max,
    "for Canada, Ontario and Waterloo Region. All three fell from the late",
    "1990s to a low around 2014 and have risen part of the way back since.",
    "Canada is highest throughout, Ontario lowest, and Waterloo Region sits",
    "between them, closer to Ontario."
  ),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5,
  phone = list(scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 10),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: crime-chart-function

# The nine offence charts below replicate the Globe and Mail's last two
# charts, split into one chart per offence with Canada, Ontario and the Region
# as the three lines, like the CSI charts above. Each offence has two tabs:
# the rate per 100,000 people as published ("Incidents") and that rate as an
# index ("Index", 100 = the base-year rate). Every tab is one chunk calling
# crime_chart(), so the eighteen charts cannot drift apart in style; it is
# the ggline template (with the hover layers of the CSI charts) wrapped in a
# function.

# Built on the first call and reused: the offences' names and base years
crime_info <- crime_rates |>
  distinct(ucr_code, violation, base_year, first_year = year) |>
  summarise(first_year = min(first_year), .by = c(ucr_code, violation, base_year))

crime_chart <- function(code, measure = c("incidents", "index")) {
  measure <- match.arg(measure)
  info <- crime_info |> filter(ucr_code == code)

  plot_data <- crime_rates |>
    filter(ucr_code == code) |>
    mutate(
      region = factor(region, levels = csi_groups),
      value = if (measure == "incidents") incidents_per_100k else index,
      hover_id = str_glue("{code}-{measure}-{region}-{year}"),
      tooltip = if (measure == "incidents") {
        str_glue(
          "<b>{region}</b><br>{violation}<br>{year}<br>",
          "Rate: {label_number(accuracy = 0.01, big.mark = ',')(incidents_per_100k)} per 100,000<br>",
          "Incidents: {label_number(big.mark = ',')(incidents)}"
        )
      } else {
        str_glue(
          "<b>{region}</b><br>{violation}<br>{year}<br>",
          "Index: {label_number(accuracy = 1)(index)} ({base_year} = 100)<br>",
          "Rate: {label_number(accuracy = 0.01, big.mark = ',')(incidents_per_100k)} per 100,000"
        )
      }
    )

  x_min <- plot_data |> pull(year) |> min()
  x_max <- plot_data |> pull(year) |> max()
  # Breaks every 5 years (every 10 on a phone) for the long series; the
  # 2015-on series is short, so it keeps 5 on a phone too
  x_breaks <- seq(ceiling(x_min / 5) * 5, x_max, 5)
  phone_breaks <- if (x_max - x_min > 15) seq(2000, x_max, 10) else x_breaks

  # Every label placed automatically (see cwr_line_labels() in theme_cwr.R):
  # clear of the other lines, the gridlines and each other.
  label_data <- cwr_line_labels(
    plot_data, x = year, y = value, group = region,
    limits = c(0, NA),
    bold = cwr_region
  )

  # Notes for the two offences whose years or base differ from the rest
  notes <- c(
    if (info$first_year > min(crime_rates$year)) {
      str_glue("Shown from {info$first_year}: Criminal Code changes make earlier years incomparable")
    },
    if (measure == "index" && info$base_year != info$first_year) {
      str_glue(
        "Indexed to {info$base_year}: the {cwr_region} recorded no incidents in ",
        "{str_flatten_comma(seq(info$first_year, info$base_year - 1), ' or ')}"
      )
    }
  )

  # Rates are Statistics Canada's own; the index is worked out here
  caption <- cwr_caption(
    c("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0177-01", "Table 35-10-0180-01"),
    credit = measure == "index",
    notes = notes
  )

  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = year, y = value, colour = region)) +

    geom_label(
      data = label_data,
      aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fontface = fontface, vjust = vjust),
      colour = "grey30",
      fill = "white",
      linewidth = 0,
      size = 3.2,
      hjust = 0.5,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +

    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

    # Hover dots under hover targets, as in the CSI charts
    geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id = hover_id), size = 2.5, alpha = 0) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
      shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = x_breaks,
      labels = label_number(big.mark = "", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
      minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05)),
      position = "bottom"
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, NA),
      position = "right",
      labels = label_number(big.mark = ","),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values = csi_colours,
      guide = "none"
    ) +

    guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +

    # Right-axis label positioning: sit labels above gridlines
    theme(
      axis.text.y.right = element_text(
        size = rel(1),
        hjust = 1.0,
        vjust = -0.5,
        margin = margin(r = 12, l = -20)
      )
    ) +

    # The offence is named in the placeholder so the eighteen charts can be
    # told apart until the titles are written
    labs(
      title = str_glue("Title: {info$violation}"),
      subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when<br>",
      caption = caption
    )

  # Alt text built from the data: what is shown, and the first and last values
  ends <- plot_data |>
    filter(year %in% c(x_min, x_max)) |>
    arrange(year, region) |>
    mutate(entry = paste(region, label_number(accuracy = if (measure == "index") 1 else 0.1, big.mark = ",")(value))) |>
    summarise(entries = str_flatten_comma(entry), .by = year)
  what <- if (measure == "incidents") {
    str_glue("the rate of {str_to_lower(info$violation)} per 100,000 people")
  } else {
    str_glue("the rate of {str_to_lower(info$violation)} as an index, {info$base_year} = 100")
  }

  cwr_interactive(
    p, str_glue("fig-crime-{code}-{measure}"),
    alt = str_glue(
      "Line chart of {what}, for Canada, Ontario and the Region, {x_min} to {x_max}. ",
      "In {x_min}: {ends$entries[1]}. In {x_max}: {ends$entries[2]}."
    ),
    height = 5, phone_height = 4.5,
    phone = list(scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = phone_breaks,
      minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
    ))
  )
}
```

### Sources

```{r}
#| label: sources
```
